:::

::: {.tldr}
A **checkpointer** saves the graph's state after every step, under a **thread id**. Call the agent again with the same thread id and it picks up where it left off, with the whole conversation. A new thread id starts from scratch. This is short-term memory, and it is also what makes pausing and resuming an agent possible.
:::

## Reducer vs checkpointer

These two are easy to confuse, and they work together.

| | Reducer (`operator.add` on `messages`) | Checkpointer |
|---|---|---|
| Answers | *How* to merge updates into the state | *Where* to keep the state between calls |
| Lasts | One run (`invoke`) | Every run with the same `thread_id` |

Without a checkpointer, each `invoke` starts from an empty state: the reducer appends to a list that starts empty every time.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  C1["Call 1<br/>[] + [weather in SF?]"] --> R1["… answer"]
  R1 -- "saved under thread 1" --> C2["Call 2<br/>[SF?, …, answer] + [what about LA?]"]
  C2 --> R2["understands 'LA' = weather"]
```

## Adding a checkpointer

```python
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

checkpointer = MemorySaver()                     # in memory: for learning and tests
app = graph.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
```

| Checkpointer | Keeps data | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `MemorySaver` | Until the process stops | Notebooks, tests |
| SQLite (`langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite`) | In a file | Local apps, prototypes |
| Postgres (`langgraph-checkpoint-postgres`) | In a database | Production, several users |

## Threads

A **thread** is one conversation. The thread id goes in the config of every call.

```python
thread = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}

app.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="What is the weather in SF?")]}, thread)
app.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="What about in LA?")]}, thread)
```

::: {.example}
On thread `"1"`, *"What about in LA?"* is understood as a weather question, because the SF exchange is in the saved history. Asked on a new thread `"2"`, the same follow-up, or *"Which one is warmer?"*, makes the agent ask for clarification: that thread has no history.
:::

Give **one thread per user or per conversation** so histories never mix.

## What is saved

After each node, the checkpointer stores a **snapshot** of the full state, with an id. You can read it at any time:

```python
snapshot = app.get_state(thread)
snapshot.values["messages"]      # the conversation so far
snapshot.next                    # the node that will run next, () when finished

for past in app.get_state_history(thread):   # every snapshot, newest first
    print(past.config["configurable"]["checkpoint_id"], past.next)
```

These snapshots are what make it possible to pause, inspect, edit and rewind an agent: see [Controlling a running agent](../control/controlling-a-running-agent.qmd).

::: {.callout-tip}
## Remember
- The checkpointer saves the state **after every node**, per `thread_id`.
- Same thread id = the conversation continues. New thread id = fresh start.
- `MemorySaver` for learning; a database checkpointer in production.
- A checkpointer is required for human-in-the-loop and time travel.
- For memory that must outlive a conversation, use the **store**: [Long-term memory](long-term-memory.qmd).
:::
